report: sprint-009 platform path (independent source review + bounded platform patch)

inputs_not_reverified_here.adt_facts_from_root: Root parsed the existing increment008 cycle003 guest ADT offline (private runs/m1-bringup-009). Used as given: cpu0 interrupts=[70] count 1, interrupt-parent 112; other 7 CPUs removed by HV; AIC phandle 112 compatible aic,1; pmgr phandle 135 pmgr1,t8103; uart0 parent 112 irq 605; timebase 24 MHz; /chosen has no lock-regs. Not reparsed by this reviewer.

findings.fact: T8103 board_config sets USE_APPLEARMSMP=1. xnu's cpu_boot_thread (iokit/Kernel/arm/AppleARMSMP.cpp) owns ml_processor_register and processor_boot, and waits for: the IOPlatformExpert to match; a child IC registered into PassthruInterruptController; IOPMGR (UINT64_MAX wait); per-cpu IOPlatformDevice nubs. sleh_irq calls PE_handle_ext_interrupt, which goes through Passthru to the child. Generic IOCPU.cpp paths are compiled out.

PDArmPlatformExpert::start builds PDArmCPU. startForCPU calls PDArmGIC_map_cpu, which returns false because gGicrAll is NULL (PDArmGIC_init is never called on Apple), so PE start fails before PDAppleAIC_init. Even without that failure, PDArmCPU would double-register processors against cpu_boot_thread.

PDAppleAIC registered only gIODTDefaultInterruptController. ADT nubs with interrupts+interrupt-parent are named IOInterruptController%08X(phandle) by IODTInterruptControllerName, so IOService::registerInterrupt would sleep THREAD_UNINT forever in lookUpInterruptController.
PDAppleAIC never unmasked a source after dispatch. Reading AIC_EVENT masks it (Linux irq-apple-aic.c aic_irq_eoi), so each device IRQ fired once.
An IOPMGR is required. ApplePMGR is unavailable. IOPMGR.h and its vtable, metaclass and constructors are exported in config/IOKit.exports.

Timer and IPI need no PD driver. H13 sleh_fiq (HAS_IPI, no HAS_GICV3_FIQ) handles fast IPIs via IPI_SR and otherwise calls ml_get_timer_pending and rtclock_intr. ml_processor_register returns pmi_handler NULL (no CPMU_AIC_PMI).

m1n1 HV HCR, from source; runtime value not observed. C hv_init (src/hv/hv.c:183-189) writes HCR without FMO/IMO. The proxyclient HV.init() then sets FMO=1, IMO=0, TACR=1, TIDCP=0, TVM=0, TTLBOS=1 (proxyclient/m1n1/hv/__init__.py:1405-1416) before hv_start. hv_start only copies HCR for secondaries; later C writes toggle only VF (hv_exc.c hv_update_fiq) and TTLB (hv_sprr.c). So physical FIQs go to m1n1 at EL2. Guest CNTP/CNTV timer, IPI and PMC FIQs are injected separately as a virtual FIQ (HCR_VF, timer gated via VM_TMR_FIQ_ENA). Physical IRQs (IMO=0) are taken by the guest at EL1. /arm-io MMIO, including the AIC, is mapped HW passthrough unless traced. IPI_SR, IPI_RR and PMCR0 are trapped and emulated; CYC_OVRD writes setting DISABLE_WFI_RET or FIQ_MODE are refused.
findings.correction: Revision 2: the first handoff wrongly said HCR has no FMO; root flagged it from the Python HV.init.

findings.fact: m1n1 hv_vuart hooks uart0 with RX (UTRSTAT.RXD/URXH from the USB vUART iodev). That suits xnu's polled Samsung pe_serial and the serial keyboard poll (serial=3) once the timer FIQ runs.

With KERNEL_INTEGRITY_CTRR, ml_lockdown_init calls rorgn_stash_range, which calls find_lock_group_data and panics with '/chosen/lock-regs not found', because the observed ADT has none. The only early-outs: -unsafe_kernel_text (DEVELOPMENT/DEBUG only; the firstboot experiment requires DEBUG) or CONFIG_CSR_FROM_DT unsafe text. Either way CTRR stays unlocked and kernel text is not hardware-protected. Honest options: (a) DEBUG plus -unsafe_kernel_text, declared as CTRR not engaged; (b) omit KERNEL_INTEGRITY_CTRR in the experiment board block, declared. Do not synthesize lock-regs.

With cpu0 interrupts count 1, register_aic_handlers takes neither the legacy 3-IPI branch nor the PMI branch (pmi NULL), so no ADT property changes are needed for CPU service. The ADT topology is 1 CPU under HV; cpus=1 is still recommended (ml_parse_cpu_topology honors it).

patch.generic_path: unchanged; the base startProcessors() is the original loop moved verbatim (test-checked)
patch.success_stubs: none; secondary core and cluster requests panic with the reason; idle is a declared WFI-only policy

checks.compile: NOT DONE. Host clang 22 and the store Darwin cross clang++ both stop in the built Kernel.framework headers (IOLib.h/OSData.h typed-allocator templates) before reaching patch code. The first compile is root's platform build.

residual_risks: Apple PE start waits up to 30 s for Passthru. No-deadlock reasoning is source-only (cpu_boot_thread waits for kIOServiceMatchedState, which the async PE registerService sets); needs runtime evidence.
PDAppleAIC handleInterrupt loops with 'continue' on non-ExtInt AIC events; an unacknowledged AIC IPI event could livelock. Not expected with fast IPIs and HV emulation.
PE_halt_restart is the PSCI handler on Apple too; reboot(2) would issue hvc/smc with no PSCI behind it. Needs a real reset path later.
Retention WFI (HAS_RETENTION_STATE, arm64_retention_wfi) under m1n1 HV is unverified at runtime.
The boot-framebuffer nub publication on M1 is unverified.
